summary: Smart Library (Perpustakaan Pintar) tested end-to-end (both backend and frontend). Backend: 17/17 pytest tests pass covering role guards (siswa 403 on POST/PATCH/DELETE books, PATCH /library/config, GET /library/stats), Books CRUD with GET-persist verification, loan borrow+return (siswa and admin-on-behalf), reservation flow when available_copies=0, reviews, library config PATCH persistence, and AI endpoints (ai-summary + ai-recommendations returned 200 without crashing). Frontend: Admin Perpus logs in → Perpustakaan page shows 5 tabs (Ringkasan/Kelola Buku/Sirkulasi/Reservasi/Pengaturan); Tambah Buku modal creates a book that appears in grid, edit/delete testids present per card; Settings tab has cfg-loan-days/max-books/fine + save button; Sirkulasi has lend-student-select/lend-book-select/lend-submit-button/export-loans-button. Siswa logs in → Perpustakaan shows ONLY 3 tabs (Katalog/Pinjaman Saya/Reservasi); admin tabs are NOT present; search/category/avail-toggle/ai-reco-button all render; opening a book card opens BookDetailModal with borrow/ai-summary/submit-review/review-text controls; borrow succeeded (loan appeared under Pinjaman Saya) and return-my-loan worked. Role enforcement verified both via UI (tabs hidden) and API (403 responses).

critical_code_review_comments: Library backend code is clean: proper async usage, dscope() scoping for is_demo isolation, correct 403 via require_roles, _id excluded from projections, Pydantic validation on inputs.

AI _ai_text uses model string 'gpt-5.4' with with_model('openai','gpt-5.4') — verify this model id is valid with emergentintegrations; endpoint returned 200 during tests so key budget is fine, but model name is unusual and worth double-checking.
